source.title: Singularity Theorems in General Relativity: Achievements and Open Questions.

accepted.question_text: How should singularities in general relativity be given a rigorous mathematical structure and set of properties, and what precise relationship, if any, should hold between geodesic incompleteness and curvature pathologies when singularities are defined by incomplete inextensible curves rather than by points inside the spacetime manifold?

evidence.quote: Some fundamental questions, which sometimes are omitted, arise at this point. How can one give structure and properties to the singularities? What is the relation between geodesic incompleteness and curvature problems, if any?

accepted.question_text: When a spacetime in general relativity is extensible and admits multiple inequivalent regular extensions, what physical criteria should be used to decide which extension is the physically appropriate one, especially when some candidate extensions remain singularity-free and others introduce singular behavior or violate conditions such as causality or energy positivity?

evidence.quote: which physical reasons are to be used to discriminate between inequivalent extensions?

accepted.question_text: Do the singularity theorems still leave room for constructing cosmologically realistic universes that are geodesically complete and free of singularities, even while satisfying the usual causality and energy conditions that appear in classical general relativity?

evidence.quote: Of course, the model is not realistic in the sense that it cannot describe the actual Universe —for instance, the isotropy of the cosmic background radiation cannot be explained—, but the question arises of whether or not there is room left over by the singularity theorems to construct geodesically complete realistic universes.

accepted.question_text: Can one formulate a singularity-theorem-style criterion based on the spatial averages of physical variables such as energy density or related matter fields, so that vanishing spatial averages distinguish singularity-free models permitted by the singularity theorems from models that still develop singularities?

evidence.quote: However, his work provided some inspiration, and I believe that the vanishing of the spatial averages of the physical variables is probably a condition which may allow to distinguish between the singularity-free models allowed by the singularity theorems and the singular ones. A conjecture of the singularity-theorem type was put forward in (Senovilla, 1998b) with this purpose.
